rationale: JPA @Entity mapped to the 'owners' table, with validated fields and a one-to-many relationship to Pet. It is a central domain entity of petclinic. Per the spec, an ORM entity class is a data-model ObjectSchema that maps to the data-store collection. It declares the mapping but performs no storage I/O itself, so data_persistence is false.

Spring Data repository interface defining read access (findAll, paged findAll) against the vets table, with caching and read-only transactions. It is repository/DAO code that talks to storage, so it is modelled as data-store access patterns over the Vet collection and is a significant persistence integration point.

A Spring @Configuration class that wires i18n support: a session-based locale resolver and a locale-change interceptor driven by the URL parameter. It is a notable framework configuration component that drives the localisation of the web UI, but it is not a core architectural boundary.

HTTP POST /owners/new route handler in a Spring MVC controller: one method-path pair forms an API operation. It validates the submitted owner, saves it through the repository, and drives the server-rendered UI by returning a view or a redirect with flash messages.

Trivial getter on the Pet entity returning a field. Accessors are implementation details, not architectural elements; the birthDate property would be modelled as a schema property of the Pet object schema, not this method.

A Spring @InitBinder hook that stops request binding from setting id fields. This is a small mass-assignment safeguard, but it is per-controller framework boilerplate with no logic of its own. It sits below the granularity of an architectural element, at most an implementation detail of the controller.

Spring Data JPA repository for PetType that issues a named JPQL query (ordered retrieval of pet types) against the pet types table. It is the persistence-access layer for one collection, best modelled as a data-store access pattern. Notable but narrow: a single lookup query supporting form population.

HTTP route GET /owners/{ownerId}/edit bound to a controller method; one method-path pair is an API operation. It returns a server-rendered form view name, so it drives the user interface. It is a system boundary entry point, but only one of several owner endpoints, so significance is 3.

A Spring @Component that converts between PetType and its form-field string, looking types up via the injected PetTypeRepository. It is a small framework-plumbing component used in form binding: an application component of minor significance. It calls the repository but does not itself implement persistence.

HTTP GET route /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/edit bound to a Spring MVC controller method; one method-path pair is an API operation. It renders the pet edit form view, so it drives the user interface. It is a notable but ordinary endpoint within the PetController.

Spring Boot application entry point bootstrapping the whole PetClinic application. It represents the deployable application component as a unit and is the system's main entry point, so it is a core architectural element. It implements no cross-cutting concern directly.

A Spring Data JPA repository for Owner that declares the store's read operations: a prefix search on last name with paging, and lookup by id. It is the persistence access layer for the owners collection, so it belongs in data-store as the access patterns issued against that collection. It is a central integration point with durable storage.

A Spring MVC handler bound to GET /owners/find, so it is one method-path HTTP operation. It contains no logic: it only returns the 'owners/findOwners' view name, which drives rendering of the find-owner form. It is a notable but thin endpoint in the owner module.

This is a trivial Spring Validator boilerplate override that only checks whether a class is assignable to Pet. It is an implementation detail of PetValidator, not an architectural element. It implements no cross-cutting concern.

An HTTP GET route on /owners/{ownerId} handled by OwnerController.showOwner, which makes it an API operation (one method-path pair). It loads the owner through the repository rather than persisting anything itself, and it renders the ownerDetails server-side view, so it drives the UI.

Vets is a JAXB-annotated wrapper whose shape is published as the XML/JSON payload of the vets resource endpoint. Because it is a serialized response schema rather than an internal DTO, it is modelled as a data-model object schema. It is a minor container type.
